diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 19871dd added a typo to chat_stream in patient/api_gateway/app/main.py. The new-session title code reads `len(req.qestion)` instead of `len(req.question)` (line 478). ChatRequest is a pydantic BaseModel whose only fields are session_id, question, collection_name and stream. Reading the undefined `qestion` makes pydantic's __getattr__ raise AttributeError. That line is only in the else-branch, which runs for new sessions (no session_id) whose question has no '?'. Only that request type fails, and FastAPI returns a 500 for it. Questions with '?' and existing sessions skip the line, which explains the partial ~5.5% 5xx rate. The minimal fix is to change `req.qestion` to `req.question` on line 478.
evidence: patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:478 - `title = req.question.strip()[:60] + ("..." if len(req.qestion) > 60 else "")` uses the misspelt attribute `qestion`.
patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:475-478 - the typo is only in the else-branch, so only questions without '?' reach it. Branch condition is `if "?" in req.question`.
patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:472 - the title logic runs only when `not session_id`, i.e. for new sessions.
patient/api_gateway/app/main.py:84-88 - ChatRequest defines session_id, question, collection_name and stream. There is no `qestion` field or alias.

Stack trace: AttributeError "'ChatRequest' object has no attribute 'qestion'" raised from pydantic/main.py __getattr__, called from chat_stream. The trace says line 477 but the code is now at 478. A line added above this code by a later commit could explain the offset, but I did not check this.
faults/acceptance/test_f5_typo.py:4-11 - a keyword query with no '?' must return 200 and currently hits the typo. A question with '?' must still return 200.
Per the incident report, traffic was flat and the error ratio rose right after the deploy containing 19871dd, which points to a code defect, not load.

patch.diff:
diff --git a/patient/api_gateway/app/main.py b/patient/api_gateway/app/main.py
--- a/patient/api_gateway/app/main.py
+++ b/patient/api_gateway/app/main.py
@@ -475,7 +475,7 @@
         if "?" in req.question:
             title = req.question.split("?")[0].strip()[:60] + "?"
         else:
-            title = req.question.strip()[:60] + ("..." if len(req.qestion) > 60 else "")
+            title = req.question.strip()[:60] + ("..." if len(req.question) > 60 else "")
         cursor.execute("INSERT INTO chat_sessions (id, title, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (session_id, title, datetime.utcnow().isoformat()))
         conn.commit()
patch.rationale: Commit 19871dd added a typo to chat_stream. In the new-session title branch for questions without '?', it calls len(req.qestion). ChatRequest is a pydantic BaseModel. Its only fields are session_id, question, collection_name and stream, so reading req.qestion raises AttributeError and FastAPI returns a 500. The fix changes the misspelt attribute to req.question. This keeps the intended 60-character title truncation with a trailing '...'. Questions containing '?' and existing sessions never reached this line, so their behaviour does not change. The keyword query in faults/acceptance/test_f5_typo.py ('hostel curfew timings') should now return 200 instead of 500.
